Agent.text:
*Hello!* Here's where things landed.

I built your own version of the web-testing tool: a dark-themed desktop app called WebProbe with the same core tools as the original — a local interception proxy that stops every request so you can edit or drop it, a full HTTP history, a Target tab that maps every site and page the traffic touches, a Repeater for resending and tweaking requests, a simple Intruder for attack runs, and a Decoder for Base64, URL, hex and HTML. The styling, hotkeys and timeouts are the real numbers found inside the original's own files, and the safety check Craft Anything runs now passes: it builds, draws a proper window, and the values sheet matches the code. Verified live: pages fetched through the proxy come back end-to-end.

What differs: HTTPS traffic is passed through untouched (the original decrypts it only after you install its browser-trusted certificate, which needs your permission — that part is left out on purpose), and the automated scanner, collaboration service and plug-in system aren't in this version. Everything the proxy sees is stored for this run only, like a fresh session each time.

One idea to ask next: "add HTTPS decryption with a certificate I approve once" — that would let it intercept secure sites too, the way the original does.
